newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela gasoline hike awaits salary rises -Matos.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela gasoline hike awaits salary rises -Matos.

text.p: A planned 27 percent average increase in Venezuela's domestic gasoline prices will be carried out when private sector workers have received salary rises, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar.
"We're going to wait for the private sector to comply with the salary increases," Matos told reporters after attending a human rights forum.
Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said Wednesday the gasoline price hike, set for Thursday, had been postponed until July 31 for "technical reasons".

But Matos indicated the hike could be delayed further and would not take place until private sector employers raise salaries and pay a "transference bonus" to workers as agreed under a recent series of labor law reforms which removed an outdated severance payments system.
The increase in gasoline prices, which will bring the average price to 70 bolivars ($0.14) per liter, has more symbolic than fiscal significance in Venezuela.
Matos said the increase would raise government revenues this year by only 50 billion bolivars ($102 million).
Under an agreement signed with the International Monetary Fund last year, Venezuela hiked gasoline prices 500 percent and agreed to gradually increase prices to export prices.
